validity.researcher_notes: Existence, classification and attribution all confirmed independently; no duplicate in the 45-row roster (only Vermont pipeline in the batch). This is Vermont Gas Systems' (VGS) 'Addison Natural Gas Project': an intrastate extension of VGS's own LDC gas system from Colchester (Chittenden County) south to Middlebury (Addison County), VT -- 41 miles, running from vtdigger.org/2019/12/11/report-finds-vermont-gas-pipeline-is-generally-in-compliance/ ('The $165 million pipeline runs 41 miles from Colchester to Middlebury, where natural gas is injected into the company's smaller, low-pressure distribution lines') and confirmed independently by vermontbiz.com's 2016 construction-progress article and the 2011/2013 proposal coverage. Because it is a purely intrastate LDC project it was never FERC-jurisdictional -- regulated instead by the Vermont Public Service Board (CPG granted Dec. 2013) / its successor the Public Utility Commission, which is the correct source ladder for this row (checked eia.gov's Natural Gas Pipeline Projects workbook directly: the only 'Vermont Gas Sys Inc' entry in it is an unrelated 1999 FERC import-capacity project at the Canadian border, docket CP97-324 -- the Addison project itself is absent, as expected for a non-FERC intrastate build). Owner/operator = Vermont Gas Systems confirmed by every source (wamc.org 2018, vtdigger 2019, vermontpublic 2021 and 2025 all call VGS 'the owner'/operator); matches the sheet's Owner1 'Vermont Gas' 100%. Completed/in-service April 2017 confirmed by three independent outlets (vtdigger 2019, vermontbiz 2016 progress reporting, vermontpublic 2025-01-09 confirms it has been 'gassed up' since 2017), consistent with sheet StartYear1=2017. Delayed=yes/DelayType=confirmed is well documented and not a close call: original CPG estimate was $86.6M (Dec 2013), revised to $122.7M (Jul 2014) then $154.4M (late 2014, capped at $134M for ratepayer purposes), and the project ultimately cost about $165-165.6M by mid-2016 (vermontbiz, corroborated independently by vtdigger's 2019 'the $165 million pipeline' figure) -- an ~91% cost overrun accompanied by a contractor termination/litigation (2014), anti-fracking protests, eminent-domain filings, and a Public Service Board proceeding to reconsider the certificate. One caveat worth flagging for the record though it does not change any owed cell: Vermont regulators' Jan. 2021 investigation (vermontpublic.org/vpr-news/2021-02-01) found the pipeline was buried shallower than approved in a New Haven swamp segment (an unapproved 'sink-in-the-swamp' method), lacked a professional-engineer sign-off, and VGS delayed disclosure ~9 months; a Vermont Supreme Court ruling (Apr. 2024) found the PUC's response to that investigation insufficient, and as of Jan. 2025 VGS has been ordered to file a new petition allowing public comment (vermontpublic.org/local-news/2025-01-09/...). None of this puts the pipeline's operating status, ownership, or physical existence/route in doubt -- it has operated continuously since 2017 -- so it is recorded here as a compliance-history caveat, not a validity concern requiring a contested value.
